baseline.name: Sort and merge directly into output
baseline.approach: Sort by interval start and append or extend disjoint result rows during one sweep.
baseline.time: Usually O(n log n) with an O(n) sweep
baseline.space: O(k) returned rows plus sort workspace for k merged intervals

archived.name: Sort, compact input, then allocate output
archived.time: Usually O(n log n), plus O(n) sweep and O(k) copy
archived.space: O(k) returned rows plus implementation-dependent qsort workspace

why: Sorting makes overlap decisions local, but the archived second allocation/copy does not remove the sort or output-storage costs of this baseline.
quantitative_comparison: Both perform one sort and one linear merge sweep; the archive additionally copies k compacted intervals into allocated output. No asymptotic or measured advantage over this baseline is established.
tradeoffs: Input pointers/endpoints are mutated. Comparator subtraction can overflow outside the bounded problem domain, and allocations are unchecked. C does not prescribe qsort's algorithmic bound.
evidence_basis: Static pass/allocation comparison of the exact source and a conventional sort-and-output baseline; no timing benchmark.
